checks: Raw depth is upper semicontinuous because a strict depth sublevel is witnessed by one closed cap of strictly smaller mass, and expanding that cap slightly preserves the strict bound by continuity from above while including a neighborhood. Every finite positive compact family has a maximizing mark at every site, and I is finite and nonempty.

For each chosen circuit, the unshifted weighted margins vanish identically on its base plane. The shift is ε(g_j−a_p)/S_j, and the weighted sum is ε times [Σ ρ_j g_j/S_j−a_p Σ ρ_j/S_j], which is zero by the chosen κ. Thus every point on the entire plane, including outside the old fiber, stays covered by at least one shifted closed cap.

At each selected cap the old aggregate mass is Q−S_j δb_j+o(ε), where δb_j=O(ε); if the shift coefficient is zero the error is zero. The exact signed identity contributes εg_j at the same threshold. Thus all new cap masses in the circuit have common first-order coefficient a_p. The hypothesis is agreement of left and right slopes per cap, with potentially different S_j between caps. There is no assertion that regular circuits exist simultaneously without this hypothesis.

At nondeep sites the accepted predecessor supplies fixed finite covers of the entire planes at budgets q_p<Q. The finite list has a uniform positive slack. Total variation at most εΣ|ξ_i| changes every fixed cap mass by at most that amount, so these covers stay below the perturbed deep budget, even when the latter decreases. When n=0 all bases are deep because there is just one.

Taking the largest deep budget and the exact denominator M+εΣξ_i gives after subtracting β the divided upper bound (max_p a_p−βΣξ_i)/M in the limit. The finite set of expansions has a uniform o(ε) error and all covers are for actual perturbed fibers.

For every signed ξ the competitors eventually lie in any Hausdorff neighborhood of the original, so local minimality makes the displayed maximum row pairing nonnegative for every ξ. Strict separation of zero from the finite row hull would give a single direction making all row pairings negative. A convex representation of zero gives the stated probability vector, including the singleton case, with dependence on the fixed selected marks and circuits.
